label: Resonator spectroscopy vs power
axes: A 2-D map per measured entity: horizontal axis = readout drive frequency (often mirrored as a second axis showing detuning from the currently stored value), vertical axis = readout drive strength increasing upward (plotted linearly in some archives, on a logarithmic power scale in others), colour = measured resonator response magnitude. Overlays: a traced minimum-response line giving one frequency per drive row; and, when the node commits an update, a vertical marker at the claimed frequency plus a horizontal marker at the claimed drive strength. Some runs additionally ship a 1-D companion — normalized response versus frequency, one thin curve per drive strength (colour-coded by strength), with the curve at the chosen strength drawn thick and highlighted.
correct_signature: One contiguous narrow band of extreme colour, clearly separated from the background colour, running across the weak-drive rows: unbroken from row to neighbouring row, a few pixels wide at the rendered resolution, and narrow compared with the length over which it stays continuous along the drive axis.
At the weakest drives the band is a straight column parallel to the drive axis - its centre shifts from row to row by well under its own width.

As drive strength increases the band leaves that straight column in ONE direction, moving monotonically, then broadens and fades into the background; a trustworthy figure contains both regimes and the transition between them, not just one of them.

The traced minimum line sits inside the band's width everywhere the band is visible, and is straight with only fine jitter over the weak-drive rows; where the band has already faded the trace is allowed to wander, and that wandering alone is not a defect.
The claimed-frequency marker falls inside the straight weak-drive column, within about one band width of its centre.
The claimed-drive marker falls in the regime where the band is still straight and still clearly contrasted against background - below where the band bends away and washes out.

The two markers therefore cross ON the band, not in featureless background; and in each weak-drive row the band's contrast against that row's background exceeds that row's pixel-to-pixel speckle by a clear margin.

failure_appearance.wrong_peak: Inferred from per-entity panels inside accepted runs where the node emitted no update for that entity - not from a node rejection: the traced minimum line jumps between widely separated frequencies from one drive row to the next, spanning much of the swept width, while the only band that persists across neighbouring rows persists across neighbouring drive rows; the claimed-frequency marker then sits many band widths away from that column, with nothing but grain under it. Also counts here: the marker sits on a short, discontinuous streak while a deeper, row-to-row-continuous band exists elsewhere.
failure_appearance.no_signal: Inferred from per-entity panels inside accepted runs where the node emitted no update for that entity - not from a node rejection: apart from grain the map is one flat colour - no column of extreme colour survives across neighbouring drive rows anywhere, and the traced minimum has no preferred position, meandering over most of the swept width. In the 1-D companion the per-drive curves all lie on top of each other with no shared dip, and the highlighted curve's excursions are the same size at every frequency, so no dip stands out from its own fluctuations.
failure_appearance.noisy: Inferred from per-entity panels inside accepted runs where the node emitted no update for that entity - not from a node rejection: within-row pixel-to-pixel speckle is comparable to or larger than the band's contrast, so the band only becomes recognizable after mentally averaging several rows; the traced minimum stays ragged with excursions of many band widths even in the weak-drive rows where it should be a straight column, and the weakest-drive rows are visibly grainier than the rest. In the 1-D companion the weakest-drive curves swing by more than the dip depth of the cleanest curves.
failure_appearance.feature_present_fit_failed: Inferred from per-entity panels inside accepted runs where the node emitted no update for that entity - not from a node rejection: a clean continuous band with a straight weak-drive column is plainly there, but the claimed-frequency marker misses it by more than a couple of band widths, and/or the claimed-drive marker lands above the bend - in the washed-out region where the band has lost contrast and the traced minimum has already gone erratic. The claim is off the feature even though the feature is unambiguous.

abstain_when: The band is clipped by an edge of the swept frequency range - it never returns to background on one side - so its centre and width cannot be read from the picture.
Only one regime is in the picture: the band is straight over every drive row, or washed out over every drive row, so the transition the claim depends on was not captured.
No overlay marks the claimed values and the claim cannot be located against the axes by eye.
The figure holds several panels and the panel belonging to the claimed entity is blank, missing, or not identifiable - never score a neighbouring panel instead.
Colour scaling saturates most of the map into one flat tone, or the pixel grid is too coarse to resolve a band only a few pixels wide.
notes:
Thin evidence, stated plainly. Six figures read across two archives and three sweep dates; every archived run for this family was node-accepted, so no genuinely rejected run informed this entry. The failure appearances above were NOT invented: they were harvested from per-entity panels inside accepted runs where the node emitted no parameter update for that entity - a weaker signal than a real rejection, because a missing update can also mean the entity was simply not targeted. A maintainer should re-derive the failure text once a node-rejected run is archived.

Acceptance is per entity, not per file. One figure file routinely carries a textbook panel next to a degenerate one, and multi-panel layouts leave large blank regions between panels. Always score the panel matching the claim's entity; blank space is layout, not missing data.

Colour convention is not fixed - in these archives the resonance reads as the dark extreme against a lighter background, with a bright asymmetric lobe on one side of it, but the judge must treat "band of extreme colour distinct from background" as the invariant and never assume dark means resonance.

The drive axis is plotted linearly in some runs and on a logarithmic power scale in others. This changes how sharply the band appears to bend but not the topology - straight column, then monotonic one-directional departure, then fade. Judge the topology.

drifted is null on purpose. The figure has no repeat or time axis; the drive sweep is the only ordering, and monotonic motion of the band along it is the expected physical effect this node exists to measure. A genuine time drift cannot be separated from that effect in a single frame, so the judge must not call drift here - if band motion looks wrong, it belongs to wrong_peak or feature_present_fit_failed, or the judge abstains.

localizer is "none": this is a 2-D map and the node emits two claims on orthogonal axes (a frequency and a drive strength). Neither can be validated by pointing at one axis alone - the claim is trustworthy only when both markers land on the band together, so this entry is signature-trust-only.

Do not penalize a wandering minimum trace at the strongest drives - that is the physics of the feature washing out and appears in every accepted figure read here.
